data.narrative:
QunaSys is a Series B quantum computing company that has raised $33M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a competitive set of 11 peers across quantum computing—3 public companies (IonQ, Rigetti Computing, D-Wave Quantum) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum and Infleqtion—though the narrow peer universe constrains precision.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable valuation approach. Using total capital raised ($33M) as a baseline and applying a typical Series B-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 1.9x yields an implied valuation of $63M. This method is grounded in observed progression patterns within the venture stage continuum. A peer-median approach cannot be reliably applied: while 5 same-sector comparables exist in quantum computing, none satisfy minimum thresholds for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier filtering (need ≥3 datapoints per filter). An all-sector median would risk material distortion given heterogeneous business models and capital efficiency across the quantum hardware and software landscape.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $53M (low) to $72M (high), with $63M as the median point. This range reflects Stage-progression as the sole quantitative anchor. Key uncertainties include the nascent maturity of quantum computing venture benchmarks, concentrated founder attribution to Tennin Yan, and the absence of revenue or technical differentiation metrics in the present dataset. Investors should treat this range as preliminary and condition further valuation refinement on operational metrics and capital efficiency relative to staged peer cohorts.
